in_latin.name: Anastellus
in_latin.meaning: Name derived from Greek, meaning 'Resurrection' or 'Rebirth'
in_latin.long_meaning: Anastellus is a Latinized form of the Greek name Ánastellēs (Ἀναστέλλης), which is derived from the verb anastellō (ἀναστέλλω), meaning 'to cause to stand up' or 'to raise up.' This verb is in turn derived from the prefix ana- (ἀνά), meaning 'up' or 'again,' and the verb stellō (στέλλω), meaning 'to stand' or 'to set.' In the context of Christian theology, anastellō is often used to describe the act of resurrection, particularly in reference to the resurrection of Jesus Christ. In the early Christian church, the name Anastellus was likely given to children born into families who saw the resurrection of Jesus as a central aspect of their faith. Today, the name Anastellus remains a powerful symbol of hope and redemption in the Christian tradition.
